en: A sawhorse and some tools can go a long way. Basic carpentry can be done here.
A dry looking grass, with numerous starchy seeds. Good for making bread, possibly?
A wild cocoa tree. It is very short. Cocoa tastes good, and can taste even better after it is processed into chocolate.
A rock on which diamonds have grown.
Space out in this bed modelled after one of the first reuseable spacecraft flown by our saviors.
A small safe, and very strong. The lock is very insecure, though.
It could be a dirturchin. It is probably not an alien sea urchin, and it is definitely not an alien normal urchin.
A cold iceball dwarf planet on the outskirts of the Sol system.
A long bar, smooth enough to slide drinks down; right before missing the recipient and ending up un the floor, shattered as your dreams, as you are fired from the establishment.
An egg of a cold, snowy white, the bottom of which is speckled with blue. Touching it reveals that it is very cold.
Nuu cannot use this. Male Nuu have to use the stall, always.
A very hot blasted rock. The closest planet to Sol.
A small rusted countertop. Dust coats the surface. You can draw smileys in it!
Turbines? Scrubbers? Condensers? It is difficult to surmise in this state.
A small battered console. Sediment clogs all the gaps.
A short plant with a blue-rimmed reproductive organ. These are called 'flowers'.
A plant with a soft metallic bulb. It is a boltbulb, surely.
A space kiwi plant, though it seems to have forgotten its domestication.
The homeworld of our saviors. It doesn't exist anymore.
An orange carrot grows below this carrot plant. Shocking, is it not?
A red egg, speckled with yellow. It radiates heat; touching it for too long would burn the hand.
This chair could have, at one point, been someone's favorite. Now it is definitely not.
A big whitish egg, covered in big black mottles; or is it a big black egg covered in whiteish mottles?
A wild sugary cane, the sap is deliciously sweet. History of sugar cane on Earth was the very opposite of sweet.
Sugar cane requres a lot of manual labor in the burning sun to farm, but many Nuu do it anyways, despite the health risk.
I wonder what use this tiny input had. There's not much possible with eight buttons.
Wires and other material hang through this punchhole in the ceiling.
Cotton prooduces these little balls of seeds and fluff, the latter used to spin textiles and other things. On Golchar, there was a type of mold used in the same way.
This durasteel bed is surprisingly stable, despite its appearance.
It is smart to have redundant inputs, in the case that one breaks. What should be done when they all do?
A gas giant with impressive rings. Atmospheric conditions cause a hexagon to form at one of the poles. Most Humans will say it is their favorite planet besides Earth.
A steel workbench. The exterior is scattered with tools.
A brightly-coloured dirturchin plant, poking out from the soil. They say it is comparable to Golchari spinewad meat, but they also say it is not even close to as good.
Red berries on a plant. Eating a few gives one a buzz of energy. It is something approximating coffee, if not exactly that.
High pressure steam once blasted through this turbine. It looks like the pressure got too high for it to handle.
Fluffy balls with sharp seeds grow on this plant. It is either cotton, or resembles it enough to be used similarly.
A chandelier made from glass and brass. It burns paraffin, judging by the smell. Not safe for swinging on in a bar fight.
A plant of a brilliant blue. They say these things are called 'flowers'!
Is it an inlet, an outlet, or an engine? You decide!
This small electric turbine blasts hot air at your hands to dry them quickly. It is not always easy to supply paper towels on distant planets.
Is it an imitation plant, or just one with very waxy leaves? It is sometimes hard to tell.
Now I have one more indescribable horror to worry about...
A space kiwi plant. Kiwis always reminded me of the stuffed vermin from home, only they are sweet and contain no entrails.
A short cocoa tree. A popular Nuu snack is made from chocolate, spores, and crunchy burnt sugar.
It seems that some of the 'R' got weathered away. Or was it supposed to say 'floop'?
Small glowing tendrils protrude from the ceiling, lighting the way.
This thing turning on at all is laudatory to its designer.
This display has been beaten off its mount. The tube has a giant hole in it.
A metalworking anvil made from iron. These are very heavy.
A copper lamp, hanging from a copper chain.
An upright piano. Someone left their drink on the top.
A sugary, orange, brittle tuber. It is either a carrot, or something close enough.
Coffea plants produce small red drupes, the pits of which should be roasted. Afterwards, you will have coffee beans!
A plant of a bright yellow that catches the eye. It is similar in color to caution markings.
A plant with a soft metallic bulb. It is a boltbulb.
Sol. The light that shone on our savior's homeworld. It does no longer.
A small rock on which diamonds have grown.
The skin of a single large animal is laid across this wooden bed as a blanket.
A metal workbench. It is well enough equiped to make a wide variety of materials and furnishings.
Wheat, a versatile starchy grain. You can make noodles and bread out of it, just like gloom shrooms!
